FateLoom / 织命录

A narrative simulation engine for fictional worlds.
Turn stories into knowledge graphs, agents, simulations, and fate reports.

中文 · Quick Start · Windows EXE · Attribution

--- ## What Is FateLoom? FateLoom is an open-source engine for **fictional world modeling, character fate simulation, and story development forecasting**. It takes seed materials such as novels, lore documents, character notes, outlines, or worldbuilding drafts, then turns them into a local knowledge graph. From that graph, it generates autonomous character agents, runs multi-agent social simulations, and produces structured prediction reports or long-form chapters. ```text Seed materials -> Local knowledge graph -> Character agents -> Multi-agent simulation -> Fate prediction report ``` FateLoom is built for creators, researchers, and tool builders who want to ask: - What may happen next in this fictional world? - How would each character react to a new event, conflict, or constraint? - Which relationships and hidden forces are shaping the next state of the story? - How can a long-form novel preserve continuity across characters, timelines, rules, and style? ## Highlights | Layer | What FateLoom Does | | --- | --- | | World Memory | Builds a local JSON-backed knowledge graph from uploaded seed materials. | | Agent Design | Generates graph-grounded personas, roles, motivations, and behavior tendencies. | | Simulation | Runs CAMEL-OASIS based multi-agent social simulations. | | Reporting | Produces graph-backed prediction reports with structured reasoning. | | Novel Flow | Supports character cards, narrative config, chapter generation, checkpoint, and rollback. | | Style Control | Extracts abstract writing-style features from reference books without copying source text. | ## Product Modes ### Fate Prediction Use this mode when you want to explore possible story futures. ```text seed materials -> ontology -> graph -> personas -> simulation config -> social simulation -> prediction report -> report / agent interaction ``` ### Long-Form Creation Use this mode when you want to generate chapters while keeping continuity visible. ```text world / character / outline materials -> story graph -> character cards -> human review -> narrative configuration -> chapter generation -> review / checkpoint / rollback ``` ## Screens And Brand The repository ships with the FateLoom logo assets used by the README and frontend: ```text static/image/fateloom-logo.png static/image/fateloom-logo.webp frontend/public/fateloom-icon.png frontend/src/assets/logo/fateloom-hero.png ``` ## Architecture ```text FateLoom ├─ backend/ Python / Flask API, graph, simulation, report, novel services ├─ frontend/ Vue 3 / Vite interface ├─ locales/ Shared zh/en locale files ├─ static/image/ Brand assets for README and public docs ├─ scripts/ Utility scripts └─ installer/ Windows installer definition ``` Core stack: - Backend: Python, Flask, OpenAI-compatible LLM client - Frontend: Vue 3, Vite, vue-i18n, D3 - Memory: local JSON graph storage by default - Simulation: CAMEL-OASIS runners - Packaging: Docker, PyInstaller, Inno Setup ## Quick Start ### Requirements - Node.js 18+ - Python 3.11 or 3.12 - uv - An OpenAI-compatible LLM API key ### Install ```bash npm run setup:all ``` ### Configure ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` Edit `.env`: ```env LLM_API_KEY=your_api_key_here LLM_BASE_URL=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 LLM_MODEL_NAME=qwen-plus FLASK_PORT=5003 SECRET_KEY=change-me-to-a-random-secret # Optional. Set to none to use file-backed fallback. TIMELINE_DATABASE_URL=none ``` ### Run ```bash npm run dev ``` Default URLs: - Frontend: `http://localhost:3000` - Backend API: `http://localhost:5003` ## Commands ```bash npm run frontend # frontend only npm run backend # backend only npm run build # frontend production build npm run setup:backend # sync backend dependencies npm run style:parser:check # check reference-book parser capabilities ``` ## Windows EXE / Installer FateLoom can be packaged as a Windows desktop app. The packaged executable bundles the built Vue frontend into Flask, starts a local server on `127.0.0.1:5003`, and opens the browser automatically. Runtime data and settings are stored under: ```text %LOCALAPPDATA%\FateLoom ``` Build the executable on Windows: ```powershell npm run build:windows ``` Output: ```text backend\dist\FateLoom.exe ``` Build an installer with Inno Setup: ```powershell npm run build:windows:installer ``` Output: ```text installer\windows\Output\FateLoom-Setup.exe ``` ## Optional PostgreSQL Timeline The default project state and graph memory are file-backed. PostgreSQL is only needed for the optional long-form timeline workflow. ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.postgres.yml up -d ``` ## Style Controller Safety The Style Controller can parse TXT, MD, EPUB, PDF, MOBI, AZW3, and EQU reference books. It extracts abstract writing-style signals such as rhythm, sentence shape, dialogue density, pacing, and descriptive balance. Safety boundary: - Reference books are used for abstract style analysis. - The system should not copy long passages, named entities, plot beats, or distinctive expressions from reference works into generated style settings. - Parser output records `parse_mode`, `parse_quality`, and `parser_notes` so low-confidence parsing stays visible. Optional parser tools: ```bash # Debian / Ubuntu sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y calibre # macOS brew install --cask calibre # Lightweight fallback python -m pip install kindleunpack ``` ## Relationship To MiroFish FateLoom is a narrative-world focused derivative and adaptation of [MiroFish](https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish), a multi-agent swarm intelligence prediction engine. MiroFish aims at broad prediction scenarios. FateLoom narrows the direction toward fictional world modeling, novel/lore understanding, character fate simulation, plot development forecasting, and continuity-aware long-form generation.
